risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation remains stubbornly high, driven by factors such as energy price shocks, supply chain disruptions, and potentially the lingering effects of tariffs. This is forcing central banks to maintain tighter monetary policy, which could dampen economic growth.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings, Federal Reserve policy statements on interest rates, energy and commodity price movements.
sources: The Federal Reserve's Initial November Inflation Forecast Has Arrived, and Things Are Getting Downright Ugly for Wall Street (The Motley Fool, November 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Fragmentation and Trade Tensions
risks.summary: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts and trade disputes are disrupting global supply chains, rerouting trade, and increasing uncertainty. This leads to higher costs, reduced efficiency, and a more fragmented global economy.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, US tariff policy announcements, trade agreements or disputes between major economies.
sources: Mid-Year Outlook 2026 Promise and Pressure (J.P. Morgan, 2026)
Global Economic Prospects (World Bank, October 2026)
Economic Compass - The donut economy (KPMG International, September 2026)

risks.title: Slowing Global Economic Growth
risks.summary: Global economic growth is projected to slow in 2026, impacted by persistent inflation, geopolitical risks, and the lingering effects of trade barriers. Emerging markets and developing economies are particularly vulnerable.
risks.watch_for: IMF and World Bank global growth forecasts, regional economic performance data, commodity price trends.
sources: Global Economic Prospects (World Bank, October 2026)
IMF raises 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% as inflation and AI sell-off test market resilience (The Asian Banker, October 2026)
World Economic Outlook, October 2026; Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices (IMF, October 2026)
Global Growth Expected to Slow in 2026 (Geopolitical Futures, February 2026)

risks.title: US Fiscal Deficits and Rising Debt
risks.summary: The US faces large and growing federal budget deficits, leading to a significant increase in national debt. This trend could put upward pressure on interest rates and limit fiscal flexibility.
risks.watch_for: Congressional Budget Office (CBO) deficit and debt projections, Treasury issuance levels, net interest costs.
sources: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036 (Congressional Budget Office, February 2026)
CBO Releases Negative Fiscal Outlook for 2026-2036 (The Conference Board, February 2026)
Economic Compass - The donut economy (KPMG International, January 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment and Economic Impact Uncertainty
risks.summary: While Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a significant driver of investment and potential productivity gains, there is uncertainty about its full economic impact, including potential disruptions to the labor market and the risk of an AI-driven bubble.
risks.watch_for: Corporate AI spending announcements, productivity growth data, labor market adjustments related to AI, valuations of AI-related companies.
sources: AI, cybersecurity and talent gaps dominate CEOs' business priorities in 2026: KPMG (KPMG International, November 2026)

risks.title: Federal Reserve Policy and Interest Rate Uncertainty
risks.summary: The Federal Reserve faces a delicate balancing act between controlling inflation and supporting economic growth. Uncertainty about the path of interest rates and the Fed's policy stance creates volatility for markets and businesses.
risks.watch_for: FOMC statements and meeting minutes, Federal Reserve speeches, inflation and employment data.
sources: What's The Fed's Next Move? (J.P. Morgan Global Research, November 2026)
The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for (Stanford SIEPR, 2026)
Macroeconomic Update: Resilient Growth, Stubborn Inflation (Guggenheim Investments, October 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Weakness and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While some indicators suggest a stable labor market, there are concerns about weakening job growth and the impact of inflation on consumer affordability. This could dampen consumer spending and economic momentum.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate, wage growth, consumer confidence surveys, inflation-adjusted income data.
sources: The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for (Stanford SIEPR, 2026)
Economic Compass - Rising tide fails to lift all boats: A jobless boom (KPMG International, November 2025)
Spring thaw, summer heat: Biannual economic outlook (KPMG International, June 2026)

risks.title: Energy Price Volatility and Supply Disruptions
risks.summary: The conflict in the Middle East continues to pose a risk to energy prices and global supply chains. Elevated energy costs can fuel inflation and negatively impact consumer spending and business operations.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, oil and gas price movements, global shipping and logistics data.
sources: Mid-Year Investment Outlook 2026 (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, 2026)
Global Economic Prospects (World Bank, October 2026)

consensus_note: The dominant narrative across these outlooks points to a global economy facing persistent inflation, geopolitical fragmentation, and slowing growth in 2026. While AI investment offers a potential upside, it also introduces uncertainty. There is a general consensus on the risks posed by elevated energy prices and the need for careful monetary policy navigation by central banks. Disagreements are subtle, often revolving around the precise timing and magnitude of interest rate adjustments and the ultimate impact of AI on productivity versus potential market bubbles.
